newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down, many investors sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down, many investors sidelined.

text.p: Thai stocks closed slightly lower in lacklustre trade on Tuesday as many investors were sidelined awaiting key central bank economic data and on worries about government stability, brokers said.

The SET index moved in negative territory throughout the session and ended 0.85 point lower at 1,094.59 on 1.6 billion baht trade. Decliners led gainers 181 to 97 while 119 issues were unchanged. The SET-50 index was off 0.10 point at 83.56.
"Investors remained concerned about local political and economic problems," said Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.
Local investors were awaiting leading economic indicators that would be released by the Bank of Thailand on Thursday.
Also being watched is a no-confidence motion lodged by opposition parties against Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa. The debate in parliament is set for September 18.
"Foreign investment continued to be thin today and there was a lack of orders from investors in Hong Kong after their holiday on Monday," Virat said.
Bangkok Bank today said its net profit rose 7.00 percent during the first half of this year compared to the same period in 1995 and topped the active list. It rose two baht to 214.

Most communication stocks fell as the cabinet approved a bill to be presented to parliament that would liberalise and free competition in the country's telecommunications industry before the market closed.
Advanced Info Service declined two baht to 334 while Samart Corp slipped two to 172 and Shinawatra Computer and Communications dropped two to 382.
